verdicts.note: Genuinely mixed. Pole_a statements: 'not a lot of room for tax increases' [S9] and outside dollars before taxpayers [S3]. Pole_b record: as mayor he voted for a 0.1% councilmanic police sales tax [S8]. His opposition to the 4-of-5 supermajority [S9] is procedural and weak on direction. 0 at medium is the honest read; -1 would ignore the only recorded tax vote.

Direction is right, but this rests on record, not only statements: as mayor he voted for a sales tax to add police officers [S8], and he lists body cameras, three additional officers and eight police vehicles as city accomplishments [S5], alongside the jail-capacity plank [S3]. Record plus repeated statements meets high. 'Holistic' in his usage still means staffing, equipment, facilities and training, so -1 stays.

Dedicated 'Protection From Tax Increases' platform page attacking the maximum levy and sales-tax increases [S5], plus forum support for (and co-sponsorship of) the 4-of-5 tax supermajority [S17]. These are two independent explicit sources and sit fully at pole_a.

Audit and transparency authorship [S11][S12][S15] and the pledge to cut non-essential services [S5] are squarely pole_a. Two things argue against 'fully pole_a', though. He champions a charter mandate that would 'force elected officials to fund additional deputies until we get to a minimum staffing level' [S6][S9]. He also wants to develop parks and trails on county land [S3][S7]. Both are mandated or new spending, so this is restraint-and-reprioritize, not across-the-board restraint. Belkot, with a similar law-enforcement-first profile, sits at -1. Borderline; -2 is defensible.

Explicit deregulatory plank: GMA restrictions beyond state law, permitting timelines, building codes, fees and zoning, repeated in the About page [S3] and the announcement [S8]. Pole_a is 'streamline permitting, cut red tape, let the market build', and he goes further than Shull (GMA, zoning, codes). It's a single plank in campaign-authored text with no vote record, so medium would also be defensible, but repeated explicit statements meet the guide's high bar.

Strongest enforcement framing in the three races: 'unapologetically pro law enforcement', 'politicians who refused to put Law breakers behind bars' [S6], and a co-sponsored charter deputy-staffing mandate [S4][S9]. -2 high fits.
